name: Linux enum
what_it_does: Read-only picture of a Linux or Unix host: system, listening ports and their programs, accounts and groups, services, cron and other autostart, SSH, sudo, risky files, firewall, credentials in config files, containers, processes, connections, sessions, kernel modules, PAM, trust files. One-page summary worst first; profiles card, full, triage. To do: write findings with a fix ID so the matching fix can be run on its own

name: Windows enum
what_it_does: Read-only picture of a Windows host: domain role, accounts and admin/RDP group members, listening ports with programs, services, autostart and backdoor places (Run keys, Winlogon, debugger keys, WMI, sticky keys), tasks, security settings, firewall, Defender, processes, connections, sessions, shares, software, events, drivers. Every source saved raw and replayable. To do: findings with a fix ID

name: AD enum
what_it_does: One read-only pass over Active Directory: every user (enabled, last logon, password age, never-expires, passwords in descriptions), admin groups including nested members, GPOs with their links and logon scripts, risky permissions (DCSync rights, AdminSDHolder, who can edit GPOs), service accounts and where they run, stored passwords (GPP in SYSVOL, autologon, unattend files). Replaces the separate AD audits (WN-05, 11, 14, 15, 16)

name: SSH enum
what_it_does: Everything about SSH on one host, deeper than the Linux enum: every authorized key of every account with its options, the effective sshd config including Match blocks, rc files, host keys, who logged in recently and from where, and which accounts the scorer probably uses. Findings point at the SSH fixes (LX-22)

name: Web and database enum (Linux)
what_it_does: Web servers, sites and web roots; web shells, dumps, .env and .git files in web roots; risky PHP settings; app versions; MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL accounts with no password, remote root, backdoor functions and trust logins

name: Web and SQL Server enum (Windows)
what_it_does: IIS sites, bindings, folders and app-pool accounts with the same web-root checks as SV-01; SQL Server logins, sa state, xp_cmdshell, linked servers, startup procedures, and which applications connect with which login (so a password change does not break the web store)

name: Mail enum
what_it_does: Mail server (Postfix, Dovecot, Exim, Sendmail, hMailServer, Exchange) and webmail app: open relay, who may send, mail users, forwards and aliases, TLS, the webmail app's version and database account, and the accounts the scorer probably logs in with

name: Splunk enum
what_it_does: Splunk users and roles, apps (the red team hides scripts in apps), scripted inputs, which forwarders are sending and when each last sent, indexes with recent data, management and web ports, and chrony: is it running and does it serve time to clients

name: Network scan
what_it_does: Nmap wrapper: live hosts, open ports, service versions; with the host list it checks every scored service answers and flags hosts that should not be there. Falls back to python, bash or nc without nmap

name: Scan diff
what_it_does: What changed between two network scans or two enum runs of one host, additions first
you_give_it: Two run folders (or the newest two)

name: Network device config audit
what_it_does: Reads saved device configs: telnet or HTTP management, default SNMP communities, weak or clear-text passwords, management open to any, any-to-any rules, default admins. Touches no device

name: Linux backup
what_it_does: Run before any change. Archives /etc, web roots, crontabs, service configs and home folders with a hash list, sends a copy off the host

name: Windows backup
what_it_does: Run before any change. Registry areas, firewall, security and audit policy, tasks, hosts file, users and services; IIS, DNS zones, DHCP; on a DC every GPO, SYSVOL and AD object lists. Restore command per item, hashes, copy off the box

name: Database backup
what_it_does: Dumps every MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL database and SQLite files in web roots; checks each dump reads back; hashes; restore commands; copy off the box. To do: SQL Server

name: Network config backup and diff
what_it_does: Saves every firewall, router and switch running config and shows what changed since the last copy
you_give_it: Host list; SSH key or password in an environment variable

name: Protected list builder
what_it_does: Writes the protected ports, services and accounts file from the scored-service list (docs/ENVIRONMENT.md) and the enum output; every change script refuses to touch what is on it. Fails loudly if a scored service is not listening anywhere

name: Backup admin account
what_it_does: Before any hard change: one clearly named admin per box with a recorded password, so a lockout is never total. Logged as a change with an undo

name: Restore and undo runner
what_it_does: Puts one item back from a backup (config, web root, database, registry area, GPO) or replays a run's undo log, newest first, with one command instead of reading RESTORE.txt or the undo log under pressure. Linux and Windows

name: Linux safe fixes
what_it_does: Only fixes that cannot break a scored service: kernel network settings, file modes on passwd/shadow/sudoers/SSH keys, logging back on, attacker preload and hosts entries reset, trust files removed. --list, --only, --skip; every change has an undo. To do: risk label per fix; read fix IDs from enum findings

name: Windows safe fixes
what_it_does: 20 fixes that cannot break a scored service (WDigest, SMBv1, Zerologon, UAC, Guest, debugger and sticky-keys backdoors, port forwards, Defender, auditing, LM hashes, Winlogon, AppInit, netsh helpers, WMI, hosts, LLMNR). -List, -Only, -Skip, -Undo. To do: move the -Include fixes that can cut off access (NTLM, LSA protection, RDP NLA, SMB signing, firewall) to WN-27 and WN-25; risk label per fix

name: SSH fixes
what_it_does: Named SSH fixes, each runnable alone: no empty passwords, no forwarding, remove keys not on the team list (kept as evidence), quarantine rc files, safe settings block. Tests with sshd -t, reloads without dropping sessions, restores the old config if sshd stops listening. Password logins stay on (SSH is scored). To do: split into named fixes; root and who-may-log-in move to LX-26

name: Admin and sudo cleanup
what_it_does: Linux: NOPASSWD entries, unapproved sudo users, polkit and doas rules, kept LD_PRELOAD (validated with visudo -c). Windows twin: unapproved members of the local Administrators group. Never removes the account running it

name: Web hardening
what_it_does: Named fixes for a web server and its site: quarantine web shells and files that should not be served, risky PHP settings, write permissions in the web root, directory listing off. Checks the site still answers after each fix and reverts if not. Apache, nginx, IIS

name: SQL Server hardening
what_it_does: xp_cmdshell and other risky options off, unknown logins disabled, startup procedures and linked servers reported, sa renamed or disabled only if nothing uses it. Checks the web store's login still works after each fix

name: Mail hardening
what_it_does: Close an open relay, require login to send, remove unknown forwards, aliases and transport rules, webmail admin pages locked. Sends a test message through SMTP and reads it over IMAP after each fix, reverting if that fails

name: Splunk hardening
what_it_does: Remove unknown apps, scripted inputs and users; management port limited to the team and scorer; chrony kept running and serving time. Checks a search and the management port after each fix

name: Windows firewall
what_it_does: Default-deny inbound; scored, protected and safe listening ports open; admin and scoring addresses allowed; allow-all and backdoor rules off. Rolls back unless kept from a new connection; -Undo restores the old firewall exactly. To do: 1-minute default countdown
you_give_it: Admin addresses; ports to allow or exclude

name: Linux firewall
what_it_does: Drops incoming connections except SSH, scored ports, listening ports, ping and the admin/scoring hosts; own chains only; removed again unless confirmed from a new session. To do: 1-minute default countdown

name: Windows remote access lockdown
what_it_does: RDP and WinRM: who may log in (Remote Desktop Users, WinRM access), NLA, NTLMv2 only, LSA protection, SMB signing. Each a named fix; one-minute countdown that reverts unless confirmed from a new session; recorded undo. Never removes the scorer's account or the one running it

name: Linux remote access lockdown
what_it_does: SSH root login (key only or off), which users and groups may use SSH, key-only for named admins. One-minute countdown that reverts unless confirmed from a new session; recorded undo. Password logins stay on for scored users

name: Account lockdown (Windows / AD)
what_it_does: Disables domain and local accounts not on the approved list and removes unapproved members from privileged groups. Countdown and undo; never touches protected or scoring accounts

name: Account lockdown (Linux)
what_it_does: Locks every account not on the approved list and sets its shell to nologin. Countdown and undo; never touches protected or scoring accounts

name: Linux password rotation
what_it_does: New random passwords for every account with a usable password; protected and scoring accounts skipped; new passwords only in a mode-600 file. To do: countdown for the account running it

name: Windows password rotation
what_it_does: New passwords for every enabled local account, or every domain user on a DC; skips service accounts, SPNs, protected and built-in accounts; -Exclude, -Users, -Passwords; each change tested. To do: countdown for the account running it

name: Network device password rotation
what_it_does: Changes the login password on each firewall, router and switch through a kept-open session, tests it from a second session, and puts the old one back if it fails
you_give_it: Host list; current password in an environment variable

name: Application password rotation
what_it_does: Changes an application's password and the config that uses it together: SQL Server logins, MySQL users, the Splunk admin, the webmail and web store database users, CMS admins. Checks the application still works, reverts if not

name: Credential sheet
what_it_does: Merges every rotation's output into one printable sheet and a CSV in the scoring team's password-change format, then deletes the pieces from the boxes

name: Account manager
what_it_does: Add, disable, remove and set group membership for users on Linux and AD from one list: inject requests (new auditor account) and cleanup. Dry run first, undo recorded

name: Service checker
what_it_does: Probes every scored service the way the scorer does (DNS, WinRM, HTTP, SQL Server, RDP, SMB, NTP, Splunk management and search, SSH, IMAP, SMTP, webmail login, ping): check once, watch and alert, or watch and restart

name: Inject helpers
what_it_does: Small report scripts for common injects: users and groups, open ports and their programs, patch level, firewall rules, installed software, login banner. Output fits the inject templates

name: Inject tracker
what_it_does: Each inject with time received, deadline, owner and status; warns 15 and 5 minutes before a deadline

name: Run sheet
what_it_does: One page per box from the environment file: which scripts in which order, who runs them, tick boxes and times

name: Linux alerts
what_it_does: Baseline, then a check every minute: new or changed accounts, sudo, cron and timers, services, SSH keys, listening ports, SUID files, web root files, key config files. One alert per change, sendable off the box. To do: new SSH logins and source addresses; the shared alert format

name: Windows alerts
what_it_does: Watches the event logs and a baseline: logons by a new user or from a new address (RDP, WinRM, SMB), new accounts, users added to admin groups, new services and scheduled tasks, logs cleared, Defender or firewall turned off. Same alert format as LX-40, sendable off the box

name: Splunk forwarding and alert searches
what_it_does: Installs or repairs the Splunk forwarder on each box and points it at the Splunk server, then adds saved searches for the same events as LX-40 and WN-44. Keeps splunk-query fed with data

name: Brute-force and spam banning
what_it_does: Counts login failures per address in SSH, mail, web and PAM logs and bans with a self-expiring firewall entry; never bans the scorer, the box or the gateway

name: Persistence hunter (Linux)
what_it_does: Every place malware survives a reboot: cron, systemd units and timers, rc files, shell profiles, ld.so.preload, PAM modules, MOTD scripts, udev rules. Apply mode quarantines what is not approved, with undo

name: Persistence hunter (Windows)
what_it_does: Run keys, services, tasks, WMI subscriptions, startup folders, Winlogon and IFEO keys, AppInit, accessibility-tool swaps, password filters, security packages, hidden tasks. Same apply mode

name: Session and credential purge
what_it_does: For one user or everyone: ends SSH, RDP, WinRM and console sessions, drops Kerberos tickets, clears cached credentials, invalidates web sessions. Run together with password rotation. Never ends the session running it

name: Shell library (lib.sh)
what_it_does: Shared code for every Unix script: options, dry run and apply, logs, backup with undo, protected list, exit codes, password generator, quarantine. To do: the shared countdown-and-revert helper

name: PowerShell library (lib.ps1)
what_it_does: The same for PowerShell 2.0 and later, plus a CSV writer and WMI fallbacks. To do: the shared countdown-and-revert helper

name: Build step
what_it_does: Copies the library into each script so every file runs standalone, and writes a hash list of the kit

name: Linux fan-out
what_it_does: Copies the kit to every Linux host over SSH, checks its hash, runs one script on many hosts at once, collects each host's output and exit code

name: Local runner
what_it_does: Run by hand on one host (USB, share or pasted loader): detects the OS and role, runs the scripts for that box in order with a pause before each stage, saves everything in one folder
